subject: Dedicated reservation options — Mediform capacity proposal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen@mediform.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reservation proposal — initial options

Hi Helen —

Great speaking yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a concise set of reservation options that map to the throughput targets you shared (peak 350 rps inference across text and chat mix). I tried to keep three clean commitment options so you can weigh cost predictability vs flexibility. High level:

Option A — Lean guaranteed (lowest commitment)
- Cluster: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared tenancy in Dedicated pool)
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 2 (warm, pre-provisioned)
- Burst capacity: up to 6 GPUs for 30% of peak traffic windows (auto-burst)
- Ramp: 4 weeks to full steady-state; 1 week pilot
- Typical latency SLO: p95 < 120ms
- Notes: best for small production pilots and bounded growth

Option B — Balanced commitment (recommended for 12–18 month growth)
- Cluster: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated tenant)
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8 (reserved, billed monthly)
- Burst capacity: additional 8 GPUs via burst pool (pay-as-you-go pricing outside commit)
- Ramp: 6–10 weeks with staged canary traffic (we recommend canary on weeks 2–3)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 90ms
- Notes: good mix of cost efficiency and headroom; supports steady ramp to Series B growth

Option C — Aggressive (throughput-first)
- Cluster: 28x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated tenant)
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 20
- Burst capacity: additional 12 GPUs (full isolation)
- Ramp: 10–16 weeks with parallel staging environments
- Latency SLO: p95 < 60ms
- Notes: for large-scale migration and HA across regions; includes priority scheduling and extended SLA

Attached: mediform_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), mediform_dedicated_proposal_v1.xlsx (cost model). I included a simple ramp diagram in the PDF.

Next steps: if you can flag which option is closest to your procurement comfort, we’ll return a tailored term sheet and a recommended canary plan (and estimated savings if you convert burst usage to committed GPUs).

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189
Redwood Inference

From: Helen Park <helen@mediform.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@mediform.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:14:21 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation proposal — initial options

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs before I take to procurement: 

1) For Option B you list 12 GPUs with min guaranteed 8 — what is the exact billing model for the 4 non-guaranteed GPUs? Are they pay-as-you-go at a higher slot rate or billed as burst blocks?
2) Can we start the canary with 4 GPUs for two weeks instead of a full pilot? That would make it easier to get the first sign-off.
3) What happens if we exceed burst limits in a sustained way? Any auto-scaling policies or automatic recommendations you provide?

Also, Rajiv (cc) — this is the reference state; procurement will want the month-by-month charge breakdown and cancellation terms. Marcus, can you add a cancellation window and an example month-by-month invoice for Option B?

-Helen
Helen Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Mediform Health
helen@mediform.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated reservation proposal — Mediform questions (need pricing guidance)

Folks — forwarding Helen's questions (copied below) and the current Option B cost model. Quick summary: Helen wants clarity on how the non-guaranteed 4 GPUs are billed and whether we can allow a smaller canary (4 GPUs for two weeks). Procurement will need month-by-month invoice examples and cancellation terms.

Specific asks from me: 
- Approve a formal response that offers: (1) pay-as-you-go at burst rate for the 4 non-guaranteed GPUs (rate shown in attached xlsx) OR (2) convert those 4 GPUs to a short-term add-on (30-day minimum) at a blended rate (we can discount). Which do we prefer to present?
- Approve a one-time onboarding discount for Option B to help them commit: I propose 15% off month 1 committed billing if they sign within 10 business days. Is 15% okay?
- Confirm we can document a 30-day cancellation window after month 3 for Option B (standard wording: 30-day notice, no refunds for prior months).

Quoted from Helen's email: 
> For Option B you list 12 GPUs with min guaranteed 8 — what is the exact billing model for the 4 non-guaranteed GPUs?
> Can we start the canary with 4 GPUs for two weeks instead of a full pilot?

Attachments: mediform_dedicated_proposal_v1.xlsx (cost model)

Appreciate a quick turnaround — Helen is on a tight procurement calendar.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen@mediform.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@mediform.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Revised Option B terms and DocuSign — Mediform

Hi Helen & Rajiv —

Thanks for the quick feedback and for flagging procurement needs. Per internal alignment (cc: Monica, Evelyn), here are the clarified Option B terms and an attached month-by-month invoice example. Summary below — please see attached XLSX and the DocuSign link for the commitment amendment.

Revised Option B (balanced commitment) — final terms we recommend presenting to procurement:
- Cluster: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8 (billed as committed capacity monthly)
- Non-guaranteed 4 GPUs: delivered as burst capacity at a pay-as-you-go burst rate by default (line item: Burst-4 @ $0.36/GPU-hour).
- Option: convert Burst-4 to a 30-day add-on at a blended rate (BurstAdd-On-30d) if you anticipate sustained usage; blended rate: $0.28/GPU-hour for any converted period.
- Pilot/canary: we can support a reduced canary of 4 GPUs for 2 weeks (recommendation: use Option B's friendly canary with reduced traffic profile; no change to billing other than actual usage for burst slots).
- Sustained over-burst: if sustained burst > 40% of committed capacity over a 30-day window, Redwood will flag and suggest conversion to committed GPUs; no automatic forced conversion — customer consent required.
- Cancellation: 30-day notice after month 3; no retroactive refunds for prior committed months.
- Onboarding discount: 15% off month 1 committed billing if signed within 10 business days from today (expires 2030-01-30).

Attachments: mediform_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf, mediform_dedicated_proposal_v1.xlsx, mediform_capacity_diagram.png
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/12345MEDFORM
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1142

Helen — if this aligns I'll issue the amendment and final term sheet via DocuSign. Rajiv — happy to loop legal/finance if you want different cancellation language.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
